jobs.title: Engineering Internship - Lab Focus (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Thermal Laboratory Engineering Intern – Liquid Cooling Job Description: The intern will assist the Dearborn Laboratory team in supporting testing, validation, and data analysis activities for Vertiv's liquid cooling products and thermal management systems. Responsibilities include test setup, instrumentation, data collection, troubleshooting, and reporting of test results. The intern will gain hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, thermal testing methodologies, and product validation processes while working alongside engineers and technicians to support new product development and sustaining engineering activities. Preferred Major/Field of Study: Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or other related Engineering disciplines Preferred Year: Junior or Senior Tools/Skills Exposure: Data acquisition systems, laboratory instrumentation, Microsoft Excel, test equipment, thermal measurement devices, and engineering documentation systems Responsibilities: Support thermal and liquid cooling product testing in laboratory environments. Assist with the setup, operation, and maintenance of test equipment and instrumentation. Collect, analyze, and document test data for engineering review. Create test reports, summaries, and presentations of laboratory findings. Help develop and improve test procedures, work instructions, and laboratory documentation. Support troubleshooting of test setups, products, and instrumentation issues. Verify product performance against engineering specifications and requirements. Assist engineers with test design, execution, and data reduction activities. Perform routine calibration checks and ensure compliance with laboratory safety practices. Collaborate with engineering, product development, and laboratory personnel to support ongoing projects. Participate in new product development testing, validation, and continuous improvement initiatives. Maintain accurate records of testing activities and laboratory results. Qualifications: Desired Skills: Experience with laboratory testing, data collection, and technical analysis. Familiarity with engineering instrumentation such as thermocouples, pressure sensors, flow meters, power analyzers, or data acquisition systems. Experience using Microsoft Excel for data analysis and reporting. Basic understanding of thermal systems, fluid flow, heat transfer, or mechanical systems. Requirements: Pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. Strong interest in hands-on laboratory testing and product validation. Experience with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel. Ability to analyze data and communicate technical findings clearly. Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, and test procedures. Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills. Ability to work safely around laboratory equipment and test systems. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong attention to detail and organizational abilities. Ability to work effectively in a team environment while managing individual assignments. What You'll Gain Hands-on experience with liquid cooling and thermal management technologies. Exposure to real-world product validation and testing processes. Experience working with advanced laboratory instrumentation and data acquisition systems. Opportunities to collaborate with engineers, technicians, and product development teams. Insight into the development and qualification of mission-critical thermal solutions for data center applications.

Depending on the internship assignment, the intern may work alongside engineers, scientists, or industry professionals to contribute to various projects related to their area of study. Under guided supervision, interns will assist with various projects and tasks, contributing to the organization's goals while learning from experienced professionals in the field. jobs.title: Civil and Structural Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Ground Systems Deployment Team The Ground Systems Deployment and Construction team is responsible for turning bare ground into functional drone charging sites! We’re a broad, cross-functional team with skills across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction engineering with a mandate to deliver world-class construction execution with zero issues in the first 30 days, on-time and on-budget, using scalable, cost-optimized, and serviceable designs. The Role As a Civil/Structural Engineer Intern on the Ground Systems Deployment team, you will support the rollout of Zipline’s site infrastructure across multiple metros and help shape how UAS infrastructure integrates with the built environment—not just for Zipline, but for our customers and the industry as a whole. You will contribute to developing standards for charging sites and support the structural engineering of ground systems hardware and site infrastructure needed to secure permits and approvals for new Zipline sites. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including Real Estate & Development, Systems Engineering, and Tower Engineering, to ensure that site layouts and infrastructure meet Zipline’s engineering requirements as well as applicable municipal codes and permitting standards. This position is based at our headquarters in South San Francisco. What You'll Do Support the civil and structural design of new Zipline sites, including charging infrastructure, foundations, equipment pads, and other ground-system elements. Perform structural calculations and help develop drawings and design documentation that support permitting, construction, and site deployment. Help create and improve reusable design standards for charging sites and ground-system hardware, then adapt those standards to real-world site constraints. Support permitting and regulatory reviews by helping address comments and coordinate with municipalities, inspectors, consultants, and other external partners. Collaborate with teams across Real Estate & Development, Systems Engineering, Tower Engineering, construction, and deployment to understand how engineering decisions affect site layout, constructability, and operations. Evaluate site-specific engineering challenges and develop practical solutions that improve safety, constructability, cost, and speed of deployment. Gain hands-on experience taking infrastructure from early site concepts through permitting and construction, while learning how civil and structural engineering is applied to a rapidly scaling UAS network. What You'll Bring You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in Civil or Structural Engineering. Master's and PhD students are also eligible. Proficiency in Bluebeam and drafting software such as AutoCAD or Revit. Excellent communications and problem solving skills. Bonus: Experience working with building codes and developing site plans. The individual will be based at Zipline’s headquarters in San Francisco, with possible travel to the DWF area in Texas. An open mind to help us bring Zipline’s service to new and existing customers! What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). The hourly rate for this internship is $44 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. jobs.title: Automation & Controls Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Automation & Controls Engineering Intern (Summer 2027) As an Automation & Controls Engineering Intern, you’ll help build the automated test infrastructure used to shake, heat, cool, evacuate, and otherwise stress satellite hardware during environmental testing. From electrical control systems and safety interlocks to test automation software and telemetry pipelines, your work will help enable safe, reliable, and repeatable spacecraft testing. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, collaborating with experienced engineers and technicians from early design and prototyping through commissioning, validation, and operational support. Role Support the design, build, integration, and commissioning of automated test systems for spacecraft hardware and ground-support equipment Assist with electrical controls hardware, including control panels, wiring, sensors, actuators, relays, power distribution, DAQ systems, and safety interlocks Collaborate with environmental test, mechanical, electrical, reliability, manufacturing, and software teams to build safe and repeatable test solutions Requirements Currently pursuing a B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, or a related technical degree Experience through coursework, projects, research, internships, clubs, or personal work in one or more of the following areas: Electrical circuits, instrumentation, sensors, or data acquisition Embedded systems, PLCs, or industrial automation Control systems, state machines, or hardware/software integration Strong proficiency in Python Willingness to work in a lab or factory environment and perform hands-on hardware tasks The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. jobs.title: Process Engineering Summer 2027 Intern
jobs.body: About Helion We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. Our vision is a world with clean, reliable, and affordable energy for everyone. Since Helion's founding in 2013, we have raised $1.5 billion from long-time investors such as Sam Altman, Mithril, and Capricorn Investment Group as well as new investors including Thrive Capital, LightSpeed Venture Capital, SoftBank, and others to propel us forward. Our current prototype, Polaris, has reached record-breaking plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius (13 keV). Helion is continuing to iterate and on the path to the world's first fusion power plant, Orion. This is a pivotal time to join Helion. You will tackle real-world challenges with a team that prizes urgency, rigor, ownership, and a commitment to delivering hard truths – values essential to achieving what no one has before. Together, we will change the future of energy, because the world can't wait. What You Will Be Doing: Helion’s Fuel Cycle Team is focused on recycling gas from the machine’s vacuum system, separating unspent fuel from fusion byproducts. As an intern, you will work on these separation systems, learning the technology and related systems (vacuum, cryogenics, etc.). Your tasks will include optimizing system parameters, designing experiments, collecting and analyzing data, and modifying the test setup. At the end of the internship, you will present your findings and recommendations. This is a 12-week onsite internship at our Everett, WA office. You Will: - Learn and operate a separation technology used in Helion’s fuel cycle, while understanding the system on a conceptual level - Adhere to safety protocols and gain hands-on experience with the system operation - Optimize specific system parameters and present a report detailing your process and results at the end of the internship - Explore and/or implement system improvements and conduct independent experiments to further enhance the technology Required Skills: - Ability to work full time, onsite in Everett, WA for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks during summer 2027 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s, Master's or PHD in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Nuclear Engineering - GPA of 3.0 or above - Strong understanding of engineering principles like thermodynamics, fluids, mass transfer, heat transfer, and mechanics - Proficiency in data analysis and familiarity with software tools (MATLAB, Python, Excel) - Ability to learn how a system operates and run it independently - Basic understanding of chemistry and steady-state systems (undergraduate level) #LI-Onsite #LI-TM1 Pay range: $48 per hour.

jobs.body: About Helion We are a fusion power company based in Everett, WA, with the mission to build the world's first fusion power plant, enabling a future with unlimited clean electricity. You Will: - Assist in the research and development of new materials, including polymers, metals, ceramics, and composites - Conduct experiments to test the properties and performance of materials under various conditions - Analyze data from material tests and experiments to identify trends and optimize material properties - Support the characterization of materials using techniques such as microscopy, spectroscopy, and mechanical testing - Contribute to the documentation and reporting of research findings, including technical reports and presentations - Participate in cross-functional team meetings to discuss project progress and challenges Required Skills: - Ability to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks during summer 2027 in Everett, WA - Currently enrolled in Graduate (Master’s or PhD) degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry or a related field - GPA of 3.0 or above - Fundamental background in materials science principles, including material properties, thermodynamics (incl. phase diagrams), and mechanics - Experience with laboratory techniques and material characterization tools and a willingness to learn - Proficiency in data analysis and familiarity with software tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, or Origin) #LI-Onsite #LI-TM1 Benefits Our total compensation package includes benefits, including but not limited to: - Medical, Dental, and Vision plans for employees and their families - 31 Days of PTO (21 vacation days and 10 sick days) - 10 Paid holidays, plus company-wide winter break - Up to 5% employer 401(k) match - Short term disability, long term disability, and life insurance - Paid parental leave and support (up to 16 weeks) - Annual wellness stipend Helion is an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Test Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Wallops Island, Virginia you will have the opportunity to work alongside the flight operations crew and gain hands-on exposure to live test/launch operations while directly improving the tools and procedures that make those operations more efficient, repeatable, and safe. The Test & Launch Operations team are the crew directly responsible for launching Rocket Lab's Electron and Neutron vehicles and running the various test campaigns that feed into it. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. jobs.title: Change Management Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Internship/Co-op
jobs.body: FORGE ATOMICS Humanity faces two critical challenges: securing reliable energy and aggressively lowering our environmental impact. At Forge, we believe nuclear fission is the key to solving both at once. Today Forge is developing the technology to rapidly scale the deployment of nuclear fission. MECHANICAL ENGINEERING INTERNSHIP/CO-OP As a mechanical engineering intern at Forge, you'll own real hardware on Ember, our 25 MWe nuclear reactor — not a side project. Interns are embedded directly in one of our mechanical teams — components (valves, control-rod drive mechanisms, heat exchangers), fluids (primary and secondary loops, steam generation, heat rejection), or reactor structures (pressure vessel and internals) — and matched to a team based on your interests and experience. You'll design, analyze, build, and test hardware alongside the engineers responsible for it, and see your work carried into a machine meant to power an abundant, clean future. Internship and co-op positions are available for the Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 terms; you'll indicate which term(s) you're available for when you apply. Responsibilities - Own a well-scoped piece of reactor-critical mechanical hardware end-to-end — design, analysis, prototyping, and test — with the mentorship of the engineer responsible for that system - Support validation of hardware with rigorous testing: thermal cycling, pressure cycling, shock, and vibration; develop fixturing and write up results in technical reports - Apply first-order hand calculations and engineering fundamentals to perform trade studies and make clear recommendations, even with partial information - Collaborate daily with technicians, engineers from other systems, and managers to develop designs that balance cost, efficiency, and deployment logistics Basic Qualifications - Must be enrolled in a bachelor's degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline by the start of employment - 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internships and project team experience (i.e. FSAE, Rocketry, Cube Sat, Solar Car) are strongly preferred) - Must be able to comply with U.S. Department of Energy export control regulations governing access to nuclear technology (10 CFR Part 810). U.S. citizenship is not required: Forge can generally host citizens of generally authorized countries (including Canada, the U.K., E.U. member states, Japan, and South Korea), and supports J-1 exchange visitor sponsorship for international students Preferred Skills and Experience - GPA of 3.5 or above - 12+ months experience of application of technical skills outside of the classroom. Prior internships and project team experience are strongly preferred. Exceptional personal projects or laboratory research can serve as substitutes. - Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic professional setting with changing needs and requirements - Experience using test instrumentation and control components (e.g. pressure transducers, thermocouples, resistance temperature detectors, relays, solenoid valves, etc.) Additional Requirements - Position will be based in the South Bay area of Los Angeles County and will require relocation if not already local. The position will be full-time in the office for the duration of the internship/co-op term. - Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary Compensation and Benefits Pay range: - Engineering Intern/Freshman/Sophomore: $28.00/hour - Engineering Intern/Junior/Senior: $30.00/hour Your actual level and hourly rate will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Interns accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law, and receive access to various other perks. Forge is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Forge is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant's capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING INTERN (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Freeform, you’ll be at the forefront of scaling production for high-performance metal 3D printed parts. You’ll work with a talented engineering team from some of the world’s most innovative companies across a range of projects to develop and refine the processes, tooling, and CNC machining workflows that enable precision manufacturing at speed and scale. This role is hands-on and fast-paced, ideal for someone eager to learn and contribute to the development of our autonomous metal 3D printing factories. You’ll focus on optimizing post-processing and machining operations, helping to bridge the gap between R&D and production. 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative individuals who love solving hard problems and creating amazing technology! Responsibilities: Support the design and implementation of scalable manufacturing processes for new hardware and printed parts Assist with fixturing, test procedures, and post-processing steps to improve part flow through the factory Help develop documentation and process standards to support production scaling Build and iterate on tooling, jigs, and test setups for reliable, high-throughput production Identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies in part, material, and data flow- and work with cross-functional teams to improve them Support early production efforts and help transition R&D into high-rate manufa cturing Contribute to CNC machining workflows, including programming, setup, and optimization of multi-axis operations for post-processing of printed parts Basic Qualifications: Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, or manufacturing engineering from an ABET accredited university or college Hands on manufacturing or build experience from internships or engineering clubs such as FSAE, Baja SAE, solar car, rocket club, robotics club, or similar Experience working with hand tools, machinery, or complex hardware assembly Nice to Have: Advanced degree (Master's, PhD) in mechanical, aerospace, or manufacturing engineering Experience with CNC machining, including 3 or 5-axis programming and/or setup Experience with metal additive manufacturing or precision post-processing Exposure to fixturing, DFM, or process validation Experience scaling early-stage R&D into production Familiarity with MRP/ERP tools and lightweight production tracking systems Familiarity with manufacturing process development in a fast-paced hardware environment Ability to translate high-level engineering goals into practical factory processes Comfortable working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and iterating quickly (comfortable building the plane as we fly it) Strong communicator who collaborates across disciplines and proactively seeks support when needed Willing to take ownership of tasks big and small, with a hands-on, problem-solving mindset Strong work ethic with a refuse-to-fail mindset Demonstrated indicators of jobs.title: 2027 Systems Engineering Intern – Annapolis MD
jobs.body: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret TRAVEL: No Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. We have a wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies. Our differentiated battle management and cyber solutions deliver timely, mission-enabling information and provide superior situational awareness and understanding to protect the U.S. and its global allies. An internship at Northrop Grumman is unique. Sure, you’ll learn new skills, explore our enterprise, network with experts, connect with thought leaders, and finish with a resume that opens doors. But you’ll gain something even more valuable: pride in what you’ve done. Join us and launch your career. We’ll support you with training, professional development and networking opportunities, and our shared vision of global security. Northrop Grumman is seeking Systems Engineering Interns for an internship opportunity. This position will be located at our Mission Systems sector in Annapolis, MD. The qualified candidate will become part of Northrop Grumman’s Naval & Oceanic Systems business unit headquartered in Annapolis, MD which is seeking Systems Engineers for an internship opportunity. Our site supports the development, test, and sustainment of state-of-the-art subsea systems. This opportunity will provide you with exposure to a wide range of advanced technologies, including uncrewed undersea vehicles (UUVs), remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), undersea payloads, acoustic and non-acoustic sensors, sensor processing, navigation, platform integration, subsea and maritime-surface communication technologies, advanced algorithms, digital engineering, and more. Roles and Responsibilities You’ll have the opportunity to work within multi-disciplined teams to perform one or more of the following functions (exact work scope will be based on program assignment and project phase): Establishing mission vignettes and sensor/platform performance models to assess probability of detection and probability of engagement in mission engineering studies Interpret top level requirements to create system requirements and decompose into subsystem requirements in support of product design and verification planning Support system architecture development to address known customer needs through efficient and novel solutioning and generation of associated design artifacts including Concept of Operations (CONOPs), trade studies / analysis of alternatives, and definition and management of interfaces Establish and integrate components of a digital design thread Plan and execute integration, test, verification and validation Support the preparation of technical and programmatic data packages for presentation to program, company, and customer stakeholders for internal and external informal and milestone reviews Develop content and present during milestone reviews including Systems Requirement Review (SRR), Preliminary Design Review (PDR), Critical Design Review (CDR), Test Readiness Review (TRR), Consent to Ship Review (CSR). Basic Qualifications A candidate must meet ALL of the below criteria. The candidate must: Be a student who is enrolled full-time and pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college/university and will be enrolled full time in Fall 2027 Be majoring in Math, Physics, Systems Engineering, Optical Engineering, or a closely related STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Math) degree. Be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) for at least 10 weeks during summer 2027. Be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite) as well as Program Special access within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite) Preferred Qualifications: Have an overall cumulative GPA of 3.00/4.0 or higher A current/active US Government Secret clearance Intern Pay Range: Bachelor’s: $20.50 to $37.25 per hour Master’s: $29.00 to $45.50 per hour At Northrop Grumman, our internship pay rates are standardized and take into account three main factors: the anticipated graduation date of the individual, the cost of labor of the geographic location, and whether the internship is considered technical or administrative. #campusjobs Primary Level Salary Range: $20.50 - $37.25 The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Production Quality Intern (Summer 2027) Four billion people do not have access to the internet. Astranis is going to change that. We are building the next generation of smaller, lower-cost telecommunications satellites to bring the world online. And to pull it off we have to reinvent microwave radio systems in space using SDRs. Work with incredibly smart people who have flown things in space before. We are a well-funded team that moves fast. No prior space experience needed, you just need to enjoy getting your hands dirty with real hardware and be ok with struggling to do things that seem impossibly hard. Our mission and our products are meant to connect the whole world and everyone in it, regardless of race, creed, or any other distinction. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we encourage all people to come join our team and bring their unique perspective to help make us stronger. Role Work with Design, Production, Quality, and Test engineering teams to develop inspection and verifications procedures Support root cause analysis efforts and implement corrective actions to mitigate non-conformance issues Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather relevant data and insights for continuous improvement in quality Support process and systems development to improve production quality Develop dashboards, metrics, and visuals to help identify and monitor factory health Requirements A passion for hardware development and manufacturing systems, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development Ability to handle multiple tasks and prioritize Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written Must be onsite 5 days a week Bonus Previous internship or coursework experience in a similar role Experience with quality management systems or hardware manufacturing Knowledge of programming languages such as Python, R, or SQL Direct electrical or mechanical design experience Demonstrated ability to debug hardware and software problems under time pressure The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Engineering Intern - SW General Summary: About Qualcomm Qualcomm relentlessly innovates transforming businesses, enriching lives and fortifying societies. Our solutions are pivotal in crafting a smarter, interconnected world. Building on our nearly 40-year history of era-defining technology breakthroughs, we deliver leading-edge AI, high performance, lower-power computing, and unrivaled connectivity. We’re proud to be the partner of choice to many of the world’s largest enterprises. Together with our ecosystem partners, we enable next-generation digital transformation. At Qualcomm, we are engineering human progress. Join Us in Shaping the Future At Qualcomm, we're committed to engineering human progress by delivering intelligent computing everywhere. We're passionate about harnessing the power of technology to transform industries and improve lives. Our early career programs offer limitless opportunities for growth, mentorship, and meaningful work. By joining our team, you'll be part of a community that's pushing the boundaries of what's possible in AI, computing, and connectivity. With a global footprint spanning over 30 countries, you'll have the chance to collaborate with diverse talent and contribute to projects that are shaping the future of technology. Our early career programs are designed to attract inventive minds, offering a platform to contribute to our long-term innovation pipeline. You'll be part of a community that values collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. Our programs provide real-world experience, technical skills, and professional development opportunities, empowering you to make a meaningful impact and achieve your career goals. Join us for our U.S. 2027 summer intern class ! Maximize Your Opportunities: Our internship hiring model routes candidates from this application into multiple project specific roles. Steps: Log Into Your Eightfold Candidate Home Account Hover Over The "Profile" Dropdown Open Settings Edit "Profile Visibility" Role Overview Qualcomm's Government Technologies (QGOV) division develops special products based on its wireless terrestrial and satellite communication technologies for the military, federal, local, and foreign governments. As a QGOV Engineering Intern, you will sit in either San Diego, CA or Boulder, CO and support government-sponsored research, development, integration, and testing of such systems, including adaptation and extension of commercial systems to novel applications and environments, as well as internal development efforts. You will work on a variety of projects crossing multiple disciplines from across the company to deliver timely results to customers. You will be responsible for working closely with other engineering disciplines to design, develop, automate, document, and execute tests. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are essential. Interns must be willing to travel occasionally and work well with others in a technical, global environment. This internship supports multiple technical tracks, including: Embedded Software Software in Test Based on your resume you may be aligned to one or more of these tracks. Please clearly indicate your interest(s) in your resume, as this is the only way to communicate preferences during the recruiting process. Minimum Qualifications Must be a U.S. citizen Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field Must be available for 11–14 weeks during Summer 2027 (May–September) Expected graduation date of November 2027 or later 1+ years of experience with programming languages such as C, C++, Java, Python, etc. Preferred Qualifications Candidates actively pursuing a degree with an anticipated graduation between December 2027 and June 2028 Track 1: Embedded Software Experience with real-time embedded software development Experience with cellular systems, including devices and applications for voice and data, and associated test equipment and tools Understanding of communications systems including both physical and upper layers Familiarity with development tools such as Git and Gerrit Familiarity with debugging tools such as JTAG, IDEs, and gdb Experience with digital signal processing Experience with software vulnerability analysis and tools such as IDA Pro Track 2: Software in Test Test automation framework design and development using Python Test design, development, automation, execution, documentation, and debug Experience with cellular systems and associated test equipment and tools Understanding of communications systems including both physical and upper layers Experience evaluating wireless communications systems through drive tests, logging, and post analysis Familiarity with application layer protocols (TCP/IP, UDP, ICMP) and network/socket communications Experience with mobile platform operating systems including Linux, Android, and iOS Familiarity with Linux, Git, Jenkins, Testlink, and Docker Qualcomm’s Internship Program Our interns join world-class teams to help define and build what is next for mobility and the world. Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world. An exciting opportunity exists for a college intern to join our RF engineering test teams at the Advanced Microelectronics Solutions Department (AMSD) at Raytheon in Andover, MA. AMSD develops, designs, and manufactures compound semiconductor devices, microwave/millimeter-wave integrated circuits, and modules for defense applications. Must have a minimum of 30 hours of credit by the start of the internship. Experience with any of the following software: Python, Labview, Keysight ADS, HFSS, Cadence Virtuoso, MATLAB, CST, Mentor Graphics’ Expedition, AutoCAD, TCAD, C++, Java, JMP What We Offer: Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Test Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Stennis, Mississippi, you will have the opportunity to learn about the Archimedes Engine test operations on-site as well as actively participate as an operator by supporting engine rebuilds, test readiness, and hardware swaps. The Test Operations team manages the activation and operation of test facilities for the Archimedes rocket engine, collaborating with propulsion teams to develop test procedures and sequencing and ultimately enabling the path to launch our Neutron vehicle. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering discipline such as Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with Soildworks, MATLAB, and SiemensNX Python and Java experience Proficient in Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing experience Experience working with pressurized systems ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Rate: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. jobs.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Computer Vision / Deep Learning, Summer 2027
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry. As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products. If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you. How you'll make an impact: - Enable rapid research and development of intelligent systems with advanced autonomous capabilities beyond anything that exists in the world today - Research, prototype, and generally assess the feasibility of new approaches - Imagine and then implement new features that unlock magic for our users - Characterize and quantify the performance of core components of the software and hardware stack What makes you a good fit: - High proficiency in C++ and/or Python and PyTorch - Demonstrated enthusiasm for one or more of the following: computer vision, deep learning, motion planning, dynamics and controls, 3D graphics, distributed systems, and tools/infrastructure - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, small team environment - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions. Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad and $53/hr for Graduate students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends. *Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position's location. #LI-DK1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws. jobs.title: Launch & Scale Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Launch & Scale Team The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online. The Role As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams. What You'll Do Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions. Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability. Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs. Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early. Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations. Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements. Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field. Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work. Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand. Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience. Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details. Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Thermal Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: As a Thermal Engineering Intern at Impulse, you will support thermal management of spacecraft from concept, analysis, and design, to implementation, testing, and flight while working closely with a fast-paced, agile team that strives to make a high-performance spacecraft from a clean sheet design. *This internship is 12 weeks long from May/June to August/September 2027* Support the development and maintenance of thermal models of spacecraft, systems, and components Support the determination of appropriate physical properties, environments, and boundary conditions Support the selection and design of thermal management hardware such as heat pipes, radiators, heaters, thermal paint, tape, and MLI Support thermal cycle and vacuum testing of components and spacecraft Analyze thermal test data to correlate models and improve model fidelity Collaborate with design engineers to implement effective thermal management strategies Support the evaluation of material properties and thermal requirements Document thermal analyses, designs, and test results Completion or working towards a bachelors or masters degree in engineering or science Ability to take project ownership and work well in a small team Demonstrated understanding of heat transfer, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics Hands-on experience designing, building, and testing hardware Experience with thermal testing, vacuum testing, or temperature instrumentation Familiarity with CAD software and ability to learn new tools Experience with Siemens Simcenter, ANSYS Thermal, Thermal Desktop, or similar tools Experience with MATLAB, Python, or similar engineering analysis software Additional Requirements: Willing and able to work on-site in Redondo Beach, CA for the duration of the internship This position may require overtime hours; interns are eligible for overtime pay. Additional Information: Compensation bands are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual level and base pay is determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities and internal equity. In addition to base salary, for full-time hires, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of stock options , and access to medical, vision & dental coverage as well as access to a 401(k) retirement plan . To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here . jobs.title: Combustion Devices Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Combustion Devices Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the team in designing, analyzing and testing combustion devices, as well as gain experience with GD&T drafting and data processing and testing. From designing and testing structures and components, to firing up new engines, to setting up launch pads and test sites across the United States, joining the Combustion Devices team is your opportunity to help launch a new large rocket for the very first time. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with CAD/CAM Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) drafting experience Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Experience with 3D printing Experience with programs such as: ANSYS, MATLAB, Siemens NX Propulsion experience ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here . Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com. This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY: For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations. Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

jobs.body: JOB SUMMARY At S&C Electric Company , a 100% employee-owned company, we help keep the lights on for people and businesses worldwide. Our manufacturing roles build the equipment that protects the critical infrastructure of the power grid, and each of our team members lends their unique skills to this crucial mission. We empower our people by providing pathways to a long-term career and support them in their professional growth by sustaining a culture founded on respect, strengthened by collaboration, and measured by our shared successes. The manufacturing industry is booming with opportunities to learn new things, expand your skills, and build a long-term career. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner! Available Shift: 1st shift: 8:00 am – 4:30 pm, Monday – Friday Full-Time Summer 2027 Internship in Franklin, WI At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices. The estimated per hourly range for this position is $22 - 30 per hour based on experience. Competitive Weekly Pay Period The Test Equipment Engineering & Maintenance Intern will be responsible for troubleshooting electronic assemblies and systems, identifying defect trends, finding root causes and maintaining equipment reliability. This role requires interacting with various groups including quality assurance, design engineering, production and Maintenance, working on common goal of creating outstanding quality products and increasing test equipment reliability. Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment and have excellent interpersonal skills. The position reports to the Manager - Test Equipment Engineering & Maintenance. The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to, the following: Troubleshooting electronics to component level. Read and interpret schematics and datasheets. Investigate root cause and propose solutions. Enter defects and repair data into asset management database. Perform mechanical assembly and wiring following provided drawings and schematics. Ability to write test software a plus. Configuration of replacement PCs for existing test systems. Implement upgrades or assist in redesigning current test systems. To select this job as one of interest to you, at a minimum, you must have the following: In-progress degree program from an accredited university/college program with a concentration in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electronics Engineering, or related field and returning to school full-time after the work session. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Ability to work independently in a service-oriented environment. Solid understanding of lab test and measurement instrumentation. Knowledge of analog and digital circuit theory and principles. Computer skills - MS Outlook, Word and Excel. Ability to read and interpret electrical/mechanical drawings.
